added.title: Director, Engineering
added.description:
Generate Capital is expanding its engineering leadership to support the delivery of complex, large-load power solutions for data centers and other infrastructure customers. As Director, Engineering, you will serve as the technical authority for the platform, ensuring that customer power solutions are feasible, reliable, scalable, and executable.

This role owns development-phase engineering design, standards, technical risk assessment, and technical readiness for Notice to Proceed across a diverse portfolio of generation, storage, grid, and hybrid power solutions. As part of Generate’s team, you will lead the engineering assessment and execution of a growing portfolio of off-grid natural gas power generation projects integrated with battery energy storage systems (BESS). You will build and scale the systems and standards that enable consistent successful project design, engineering and operations, and provide technical leadership through development, with continued technical support into delivery. This role combines project-level technical expertise, strategic leadership and cross-functional collaboration to help deliver reliable, scalable power infrastructure that supports Generate’s growth objectives.

What you will be doing at Generate Capital as the
Director, Engineering
:

Serve as the technical authority for development-phase engineering of data center on-site power solutions through Notice to Proceed, and provide technical continuity and support to Project Delivery through construction and commissioning
Evaluate technical feasibility and risk for proposed customer solutions and Generate investments
Establish Large Load development and design standards that enable repeatable execution at scale, partnering with Project Delivery and Technical Asset Management to ensure designs carry cleanly into construction and long-term operations
Lead early-stage technical diligence in partnership with development, commercial and investment teams
Oversee engineering interfaces with owner’s engineers, EPCs, utilities, and technology providers
Support project delivery teams from Notice to Proceed through Commercial Operation
Identify and mitigate technical and execution risk before it impacts schedule, cost, or performance.

Support Commercial and Procurement Decisions

Review EPC/EPCM agreements, OEM supply contracts, and technical schedules from an engineering risk and execution perspective
Identify opportunities to improve engineering efficiency, reduce project risk, and support successful project outcomes
Accurately assess islanded behind-the-meter projects while preparing for future grid connection in the design
Provide technical input during procurement activities, contract negotiations, and equipment evaluations
Provide technical input during PPA and Tolling Agreement negotiations
Interface between Generate’s DC partner engineering teams and DC tenant engineering teams

Drive Engineering Excellence Across Projects

Guide engineering execution across multiple concurrent projects at varying stages of development and delivery
Standardize development-engineering procedures, specifications and design details across the Data Center Power Solutions portfolio
Create, review and approve critical engineering deliverables, including P&IDs, single-line diagrams, general arrangement drawings, equipment datasheets, civil and structural designs, control narratives, and cause-and-effect matrices
Coordinate engineering interfaces between EPC/EPCM contractors, OEMs, and internal stakeholders across Development, Development Engineering, Origination, Procurement, and Project Management
Manage external engineering firms as part of executing comprehensive project engineering scope
Ensure engineering scopes, resource forecasts, budgets, and change management processes are effectively tracked and communicated
Support commissioning and startup activities by providing technical guidance, design clarifications, and issue resolution

Candidate Qualifications & Core Characteristics

12+ years of experience engineering power generation projects, including engines, turbines, fuel cells and energy storage projects
Experience designing and delivering utility-scale or large-load power projects
Strong familiarity with EPC and design-build delivery models, including owner-furnished equipment, utility interfaces, and owner’s engineer structures
Proven ability to balance innovation with standardization and execution discipline
Comfortable operating in a cross-functional environment with commercial, development, and investment teams
Clear communicator able to translate technical complexity into actionable business insight

Generate’s compensation packages are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. Salary decisions take into account a wide variety of factors including, but not limited to: skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, geographic location, and other business and organizational needs. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is $190,000–$220,000. In addition, the compensation package may include a discretionary bonus and other benefits, including health care benefits, retirement benefits, benefits permitting paid days off (including sick leave, parental leave, and paid time off or vacation benefits), and other benefits that must be reported for federal tax purposes. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at the top of this range.

Generate Capital is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against otherwise qualified applicants on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, creed, religion, ancestry, citizenship status, age, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or handicap, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

added.title: Vice President, Engineering
added.description:
← All open rolesEngineering

Vice President, Engineering

Toronto or RemoteFull-time

TL;DR

Company: Sensei Labs
Product: Conductor — the AI-powered operating system for strategic programs
Reports to: CTO
Team: 7 direct reports (4 software engineers, 2 quality engineers, and the Platform/DevOps team)
Partnering closely: 2-person Product team and 4-person GTM team
Location: [Toronto / remote]

About Us

Sensei Labs builds Conductor, an enterprise strategy execution platform that governs billions of dollars in program value across hundreds of enterprise programs. Our customers are Fortune 500 transformation offices, global consultancies, and private equity value creation teams. Conductor covers the full lifecycle from portfolio planning through benefits realization, with our Harmony AI layer woven into every surface rather than bolted on.

We've been in the market for more than ten years, we're SOC-2 compliant with a single-tenant architecture, and we do all of it with a deliberately small team. That's the interesting part of this job.

We launched a full rewrite of our Conductor platform a few months ago and are midway through the effort to reach Conductor Modern. Over the next year (or so), this will give us the chance to migrate all our customers and partners to the new version and sunset our old code.

The role

You'll own engineering execution for Conductor: how the team is structured, how work gets from idea to production, and how quickly and reliably we ship. You'll drive the technical strategy and architecture direction, and you'll own the machine that turns that direction into shipped software.

This is a hands-on leadership role, not a role that manages managers. With six engineers, you'll be in the code, in the reviews, and in the architecture discussions — while also being the person accountable for delivery, hiring, growth, and the team's day-to-day health. If you want a position where you can both set long-term strategy and have immediate day-to-day impact, this is the seat.

As part of our modernization, you’ll be directly involved in any remaining architectural and technical decisions for Conductor Modern and be a key part of planning for the customer migration and the ultimate sunsetting of the existing codebase.

This is the third leg of the Sensei Labs stool, along with our established Product and GTM leaders. You’ll work closely with them to shape and implement Product’s vision and to enable our GTM team to sell and deliver value to our customers and partners.

What You'll Own

Delivery. Planning, sequencing, and shipping against a roadmap you help build with Product. Predictable releases, visible progress, honest tradeoffs.
The team. Coaching and growing six engineers, running performance and career conversations, hiring as we scale, and keeping the bar high without burning people out.
Cloud platform and reliability. Architecture, scalability, cost, and operational excellence for a single-tenant enterprise SaaS platform. Uptime, performance, and security posture are yours. You'll lead our Platform/DevOps team alongside product engineering, setting direction for infrastructure and application architecture, performance and scalability, cloud cost management, and the tooling that the rest of engineering builds on. Uptime, operational excellence, and security posture are yours.
AI in the product. Partnering with Product on how Harmony AI evolves — agentic workflows, retrieval, evaluation, guardrails, and permission-aware AI behavior in an enterprise context.
AI in how we build. Making our SDLC substantially faster and more automated: AI-assisted coding, code review, and test generation; CI/CD; automated quality gates. We want an engineering org where a small team ships like a large one, and you'll be the one who builds that.
Engineering–Product partnership. Working shoulder to shoulder with Product on discovery, scope, and sequencing. You'll be expected to have opinions about the product, not just the plumbing.
Enterprise trust. Security, compliance, and the technical side of customer and prospect conversations when it matters.

What We're Looking For

Cloud infrastructure and application architecture at depth.

You've architected, built, and operated production cloud SaaS at meaningful scale — not just supervised it. You're fluent across both layers: the application architecture (service boundaries, data modeling, API design, and the patterns that keep a large codebase evolvable) and the infrastructure underneath it. Hands-on depth in Azure and/or GCP is essential, along with container orchestration on Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, networking and identity, and the observability and cost discipline that keep a cloud platform healthy as it grows. You understand multi-tenancy versus single-tenancy tradeoffs, data isolation, performance under enterprise load, and what "SOC-2 compliant" actually costs an engineering team.

Real product instinct.

You've worked in product-led environments where engineering shapes what gets built. You can push back on a spec, spot the simpler solution, and reason about customer value — especially in complex B2B software where the user is an enterprise operator, not a consumer.

Team leadership with your hands still dirty.

You've led and grown engineering teams (roughly 5–20 people) as a player-coach. You've hired well, given hard feedback, and relentlessly tuned the delivery process.

AI fluency, both directions.

You've shipped AI or LLM-backed features into production — and you've also rebuilt how a team works using AI-assisted development and automated SDLC tooling. You can tell the difference between AI that creates leverage and AI that creates cleanup work.

Startup temperament.

You're comfortable being both the strategist and the person who fixes the flaky test. You'd rather own an outcome than a headcount number.

Nice to have

Enterprise PPM, EPMO, transformation, or professional services domain experience
Experience with Microsoft 365 / SAP / Jira / Power BI integration ecosystems
Background in selling or supporting technical evaluations with Fortune 500 or PE buyers
Experience taking a mature product through an AI-era re-platforming or modernization

Your first year

By 90 days — you know the codebase, the team, and the roadmap; you've shipped something meaningful yourself; and you've given us a clear read on our biggest delivery and technical risks.
By 6 months — the development lifecycle is measurably faster, with AI-assisted workflows and automated quality gates that the team actually uses. Release cadence is predictable.
By 12 months — engineering is a genuine competitive advantage: shipping AI capability into Conductor at a pace that surprises much larger competitors, with a team that's grown in both size and capability.

Why this role

Small team, real enterprise customers, an established product, and an unusually good excuse to rebuild how software gets made. You won't be one VP among many, and you won't be managing a slide deck about AI transformation — you'll be doing it, on a product whose entire premise is helping large organizations actually execute.

added.title: Director, Plasma Infrastructure Technology Operations
added.description:
The Director, Plasma Infrastructure Technology Operations is responsible for coordinating and improving resilience, performance, lifecycle management, and operational readiness of infrastructure and infrastructure-supported technology services across all plasma centers, primarily in North America, with additional centers in Europe. Operating across a large, distributed footprint, this leader ensures that technology enables center availability, donor experience, employee productivity, regulatory compliance, and plasma collection performance.

The role maintains a comprehensive view of the technology environment within each center. While direct ownership of individual technologies may reside with other teams, the Director coordinates the integrated delivery and performance of center technology services across infrastructure, cybersecurity, applications, external technology service providers and others as needed. The leader also has direct responsibility for designated center technologies and leads the internal Plasma support team and managed service providers supporting center operations. The role operates in partnership with the Plasma IT leadership team and Plasma IT Business Partner given that center infrastructure is upstream of everything Plasma IT ships to donors and centers.

The Director also serves as the primary infrastructure incident lead and escalation point for major center disruptions, coordinating contributing teams through service restoration. The role ensures that root causes and systemic risks are addressed and drives the operating model from reactive issue resolution toward proactive identification, prevention, and continuous improvement.

Beyond operational resilience, the Director is an operational partner to the Plasma I&T Business Partner, translating approved business priorities into infrastructure requirements, delivery plans, and operational readiness activities. In collaboration with other technology leaders, the role helps maintain and execute the center technology blueprint and roadmap.

Success will be measured through reduced technology-related collection interruptions, faster incident restoration, improved lifecycle compliance, reliable technology readiness for new and changing centers, stronger stakeholder satisfaction, and a sustained shift from reactive support to proactive operations.

The role is expected to continuously improve Plasma infrastructure operations and support the adoption of enterprise capabilities including AI-enabled operations, AI-assisted incident response, automation, self-service, and modern device management practice. Several of the capabilities this leader will be measured on (AI-augmented operations, connected-device fleet management, AI-augmented service management, self-service and self-healing, AI-assisted incident response) are areas CSL is not yet mature in.

Main Responsibilities And Accountabilities

Plasma-Center Technology Resilience and Performance

Lead and coordinate resilience, availability, performance, and operational readiness of technology services supporting plasma centers.
Maintain and execute the Plasma center technology blueprint and lifecycle-management practices in alignment with enterprise architecture and technology standards.
Implement and monitor compliance with enterprise-defined service, resilience, monitoring, capacity, redundancy, recovery, and lifecycle standards.
Monitor and improve infrastructure reliability and minimize operational impacts from technology disruptions.
Strengthen technology testing and change-control discipline upstream of rollout, so changes reach the first pilot center with materially fewer defects than today. The existing waved-rollout process should be preserved. The goal is not more stages between change and full rollout. The goal is that changes are of high enough quality before they enter the first pilot so that fewer defects are found in the field and fewer waves are needed to gain confidence. This includes rigorous test environments that reflect real center configurations, automated regression where feasible, integration testing across the connected technology set, and honest go/no-go criteria at each wave boundary.
Reduce technology-related collection interruptions by identifying systemic failure patterns, eliminating recurring issues, and driving permanent corrective and preventive actions.
Maintain visibility into technology health, operational risk, technical debt, aging assets, and center-level vulnerabilities. Ensure risks are prioritized, incorporated into business and financial planning, and remediated.
Ensure continuity and recovery plans are current, tested, and aligned with Plasma Operations and other supporting teams.
Lead infrastructure delivery and coordinate technology operational readiness activities for new-center openings, acquisitions, relocations, expansions, closures, and major technology refreshes.

Technology Estate and Lifecycle Management

Maintain an integrated view of the information technology and supported operational technology environment across plasma centers, including networks, Wi-Fi, end-user equipment, handheld devices, sensors, monitoring systems, freezer-related technology, and other connected or industrial devices supported by Information Technology. Position the center technology estate to support the growing set of connected and instrumented devices coming into the plasma center environment. In partnership with cybersecurity and broader enterprise infrastructure, establish fleet-management capabilities (secure device onboarding, enhanced telemetry collection, improved remote configuration, proactive device certificate lifecycle) that the center estate will need as more of the physical footprint becomes network-connected and data-producing.
Maintain and execute the center infrastructure roadmap, incorporating requirements from infrastructure, cybersecurity, applications, quality, and regulatory teams.
Implement and support technology standards, reference architectures, configuration baselines, and lifecycle requirements established through enterprise governance processes.
Ensure the installed technology base is accurately understood and that refresh, patching, maintenance, warranty, spare-equipment, and obsolescence requirements are integrated into business and financial plans.
Coordinate across technology owners to ensure center technologies are secure, compliant, supportable, and fit for operational use, while retaining direct accountability for designated center technologies.
Treat the operational telemetry generated by the center technology estate (network health, device utilization, environmental sensors, incident and downtime patterns, connectivity quality) as a shared data asset. Contribute this telemetry to the shared data initiative underway across the Plasma technology portfolio, so center operations, quality, analytics, and product teams can act on it. The infrastructure operations team is a first-class producer of this data, not only a consumer of operational dashboards.

Plasma Center Support and Service Delivery

Lead the Plasma support organization and a hybrid service model comprising internal teams, field resources, managed service providers, equipment vendors, and specialist partners.
Ensure consistent and responsive support across the center network, with clear arrangements for coverage, escalation, dispatch, spare equipment, and after-hours service.
Establish and govern service-level agreements, operational-level agreements, experience measures, and provider performance standards that reflect the operational impact of center downtime.
Use performance data, center feedback, and service trends to improve resolution rates, restoration time, recurring-incident performance, and service consistency.
Strengthen internal service-management and vendor-management capabilities to provide integrated accountability across a complex, multi-provider environment.
Support implementation and adoption of enterprise AI-enabled service-management capabilities within Plasma Infrastructure Operations and measure operational effectiveness.
Implement and continuously improve approved self-service and self-healing capabilities within the Plasma support environment.

Major Incident and Operational Leadership

Serve as the primary infrastructure incident lead and escalation point for major disruptions affecting plasma-center operations.
Ensure significant incidents undergo rigorous root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, leadership review, and tracked closure.
Represent technology in business-continuity exercises and operational-readiness reviews affecting the plasma-center network
Support adoption of AI-assisted incident-response capabilities in partnership with cybersecurity and enterprise infrastructure teams.

Leadership and Business Partnership

Serve as the primary operational infrastructure partner to the Plasma I&T Business Partner.

Work with the I&T Plasma Business Partner to build trusted relationships with Plasma leadership, center and field leaders, and partners.

Serve as the primary infrastructure operations partner to the Plasma IT business partner. Center infrastructure is upstream of everything Plasma IT ships to donors and centers, and this role works across shared priorities and operational dependencies, not as an adjacent support function.
Establish governance across business, technology, and external partners so that priorities, ownership, dependencies, decision rights, and escalation paths are clear.
Build and lead a high-performing infrastructure operations organization focused on service delivery, incident management, vendor management, customer experience, and continuous improvement.
Develop infrastructure operating and capital requirements and manage approved budgets within delegated authority.

Position Qualifications And Experience Requirements

Education

Undergraduate degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field preferred. Related certifications, and advanced graduate studies desirable.

Experience

Experience supporting business-critical operations across a geographically distributed environment.
Strong interpersonal skills to quickly build rapport and credibility with CSL leaders and key external stakeholders.
Track record of leading distributed physical infrastructure operations at scale across a large multi-site footprint (enterprise retail, hospitality, healthcare centers, distributed manufacturing, or comparable).
Demonstrated experience leading major technology incidents involving multiple technical teams, providers, and business stakeholders.
Hybrid service delivery leadership across internal teams, field service, managed service providers, equipment vendors, and specialist partners. Track record of orchestrating a multi-provider service model to consistent standards.
Working knowledge of AI applied to IT operations (AIOps, AI-augmented service management, AI-assisted incident response) at a level sufficient to sufficient to evaluate, operationalize, and measure the effectiveness of these capabilities
Strong technical depth in infrastructure operations sufficient to assess risks, challenge recommendations, and support operational decision-making.
Strong Project management, technical change management, and use of agile methodologies experience.
Strong collaboration with compliance stakeholders to ensure overall data privacy, security controls and monitoring is exceeded
Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices and compliance requirements.

Competencies

Operational leadership and disciplined execution
Customer and business orientation
Service-management and vendor-management effectiveness
Major-incident leadership
Continuous improvement mindset
Strong collaboration and influence across a matrix organization
Effective communication of operational risk and performance
Talent development and team leadership
Financial and lifecycle planning
Ability

added.title: Head of Product & Deployment
added.description:
About Matter Intelligence

Welcome to Matter, where we are building the future of vision AI: pairing a world-first sensor that sees molecular chemistry, temperature, and 3D shape with a Large World Model that will be the most powerful intelligence engine for the physical world. This system doesn't just see what something looks like; it understands everything from a single pixel. We call this Superintelligent Vision.

Our team has delivered technologies to Mars for NASA/JPL, designed advanced sensors for U.S. Defense, and built core infrastructure at OpenAI. We are now building the next generation of space- and airborne-based sensing systems.

About The Role

Matter is hiring a Head of Product and Deployment to translate customer needs and company strategy into a clear product roadmap and reliable deployments. This leader will connect customers, commercial teams, product, engineering, and operations as Matter moves from pilots to repeatable intelligence products.

Key Responsibilities

Own product strategy and maintain a roadmap that reflects customer priorities, technical readiness, and company objectives.
Turn customer problems and field feedback into clear product requirements and prioritization decisions.
Define deployment plans, readiness criteria, and operating handoffs for customer pilots and production programs.
Coordinate across commercial, engineering, data, and operations teams to resolve tradeoffs and keep delivery on track.
Create a disciplined feedback loop that measures product performance and informs the next iteration.

Qualifications

Required

Experience leading product development and delivery for technically complex products or services.
Ability to translate customer workflows into clear requirements, priorities, and execution plans.
Strong cross-functional leadership, communication, and decision-making skills.
Comfort operating in an early-stage environment with evolving products and incomplete information.

Preferred

Experience with enterprise, industrial, geospatial, aerospace, or data products.
Experience taking pilot programs into repeatable operational deployments.
Familiarity with products that combine hardware, data pipelines, analytics, and software interfaces.

What Success Looks Like

The company has a clear, prioritized roadmap tied to customer outcomes and technical milestones.
Deployments move from planning to operation with explicit owners, readiness criteria, and feedback loops.
Customer learning is captured consistently and translated into product decisions.

Location

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires onsite work.

ITAR Requirements

To comply with U.S. export regulations, applicants must be one of the following:

A U.S. citizen or national
A lawful permanent resident (green card holder)
Eligible to obtain required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State

Employee Offerings and Benefits

Benefits

At Matter, we believe in rewarding high performance and providing the support you need to thrive. Our compensation and benefits package includes:

Competitive compensation based on experience
Early-stage equity package
100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision coverage
Opportunity to work on novel sensing, data, and AI systems with real-world deployment paths to the largest industries in the world

Matter Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds who can raise the ambition and performance of the team.
